subject: Post-call: erase pathways, backup constraints & residency impact summary
messages:
From: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmehealth.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya@healthstream.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Mar 2028 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: erase pathways, backup constraints & residency impact summary

Thanks for the clear demo today, Kimberly — Tom here. A few follow-ups from our compliance team we need answered prior to procurement:  

1) When we receive a user-initiated deletion (RTBF) what is the guaranteed timeline to remove data from active and cold storage? Please include any expected windows for backups and snapshot removal.  

2) We need to know whether PII used in embeddings or cache entries is truncated/pseudonymized by default, or if that requires configuration.  

3) Residency: our PHI data must remain in the US and never cross regions. Can you confirm how you enforce region pinning and what happens during disaster failover?  

If possible, please provide a short playbook (steps + SLAs) and an internal contact for audit evidence (SOC 2 / deletion logs).  

I attached a redlined list of questions from our privacy officer (acme-rtbf-checklist.xlsx). We are aiming to make a decision by EOW.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

--- Attachment: acme-rtbf-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmehealth.io>, Priya Ramesh <priya@healthstream.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed RTBF playbook (short)

Tom — really appreciate the time today. Below is a concise, actionable summary of how Redwood handles the three items you called out. Attaching the more formal playbook and a one-page SLA proposal.

Quick answers (high level):
- Active data removal: deletion request processed immediately; model KV cache and application-layer records are purged within the request transaction. We return a deletion confirmation ID.
- Backup/snapshot window: backups are on a 7-14 day retention cycle by default; permanent purge from backups requires an administrative purge operation and can take up to 21 days for the earliest eligible snapshot depending on snapshot schedule. We can offer a contractual shorter backup purge SLA for Dedicated/Private deployments (example: 7 days) as a paid option.
- Embeddings & PII: embeddings are stored in a separate vector store namespace tied to customer account. Pseudonymization is not automatic; we can enable field-level token masking at ingestion via a preprocessor or recommend a prompt-layer strategy for PII handling.
- Residency & failover: for Hosted customers we offer region pinning; cross-region failover only occurs under explicit policy and will not be automatic for PHI unless authorized. For Private/VPC we guarantee data never leaves the designated region.

Requested deliverables (next steps):
1) I’m attaching a short playbook (redwood-erasure-options-v1.pdf) that maps request types to timelines and owners.
2) Ben (CC) will follow up with the exact set of deletion logs we can export for audits (audit-log schema + sample).
3) Marissa will join for procurement/contractual SLA language and provide wording for backup purge exceptions.
4) Dev will confirm the configuration steps for field-level masking and a sample config.

Can you confirm the acceptance window for a draft MOU? We can get a stub DocuSign over today if you’re ready.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: redwood-erasure-options-v1.pdf (PDF stub)
--- Attachment: acme-purchase-order-123.pdf (PDF stub, provided by external)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberley Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed RTBF playbook (short)

Tom / Kimberly — brief technical compliance notes from infra:  

- Deletion confirmation IDs are logged in the customer audit stream (immutable event id + timestamp). We can provide a signed export for audit periods.
- Backup purge: note that underlying block snapshots are immutable; our purge process marks snapshots for deletion and a GC job clears storage once replication windows complete. That is why the 7–21 day window is realistic. For Dedicated customers we can provide an accelerated GC window tied to reserved snapshot schedules.
- Embedding masking: we recommend the ingestion-side masking for PII (pre-tokenization) — Dev has a proof-of-concept we can share. If Acme requires automatic masking at the model runtime layer, that will need a small engineering ticket and scoped deployment.

Marissa — can you please draft the short MOU language to offer a 7-day backup-purge SLA for Dedicated or Private with an exception clause for in-flight snapshots? We’ll keep Hosted defaults documented as 14–21 days.

Tom — attach your privacy officer’s redlines and we’ll convert into trackable items for procurement/legal.

— Ben
Head of Privacy Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Next steps & timeline — action items for Acme procurement

Tom — thanks again. Per our internal sync we propose the following timeline so procurement can proceed:  

- Today (Fri): Kimberly to send MOU stub and proposed SLA wording via DocuSign.
- Mon: Ben to provide sample audit-log export and deletion confirmation schema.
- Tue: Dev to deliver ingestion masking PoC and a short runbook for configuration.
- Wed: Marissa to share contract clause language for the 7-day backup purge option (Dedicated/Private) and list of exceptions.

Please confirm that Acme can sign the MOU by Tue COB. If you need a technical review call, we can schedule a 30-minute slot Mon or Tue.

If you prefer, I can route a DocuSign for signature now and we’ll wait for your countersign — happy to accommodate whichever speeds you up.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
